description: Fixture registry for the Tier 2 agent-run extension defined in benchmarks/AGENT-EVAL-PROTOCOL.md (sections 2.1 and 4 item 4): measured baseline-versus-Solve-Context agent runs on the pinned real-source corpus and the independent external subsets. Tier 2 fixtures are derived one-to-one from benchmarks/context-repository-v1.json (four tasks on saiidz/solvelang sources pinned at commit c36f2b18e3393b8174943e01b79d56c65ce83c58) and from benchmarks/independent/axios-v1.json, chalk-v1.json, node-fetch-v1.json and preact-v1.json (eleven tasks on pinned external MIT snapshots). This registry is a separate suite from agent-eval-v1: its matrix is generated and summarized on its own, and a Tier 2 summary alone cannot complete benchmark evidence, because the report contract requires measured pairs in every category including cross-agent-handoff, which Tier 2 does not contain. The registry pins the contract category, a written categoryBasis, the agents, and the repetition count for every cell. Categories were assigned by the deliverable each task measures: output-driven fault diagnosis is ci-log-diagnosis; a JSON-semantics review is json-heavy-tool-output; a behavior verdict on one named mechanism is github-issue-triage; cross-file flow tracing is multi-file-refactor. No Tier 2 task requests an edit, so monorepo-bug-fix is intentionally unused, and no Tier 2 task is a handoff. Changing any fixture, category, or repetition count requires a reviewed new registry revision. Each fixture's revisionSha256 is computed by the matrix generator from the canonical JSON of its pinned source case; it is never copied by hand. The registry format schema is unchanged from Tier 1; the tier lives in this suiteId and in each fixture's tier field.

fixtures.categoryBasis: The case's subject is JSON text itself: serializeJsonLd escaping and the JSON.parse roundtrip. The contract's JSON category is assigned because success turns on exact reasoning about JSON serialization semantics. Unlike Tier 1's JSON fixture (inspection of JSON tool output), this cell measures JSON-correctness review; the distinction is recorded here rather than hidden.

No edit is requested; the contract's multi-file category is assigned because the measured skill is cross-file flow tracing -- following a behavior across the files it spans, the same comprehension a multi-file refactor depends on. The changed path sits in one file and the required evidence spans the flow's participants.

The task is fault diagnosis from the program's own emitted output: a fatal startup failure whose stderr names the process.exit path. The contract's diagnosis category covers output-driven fault finding; the output here is process stderr rather than a CI log, recorded plainly.

workspaceMaterialization.rule: Adaptation of AGENT-EVAL-PROTOCOL.md section 2.2 to pinned corpora whose sources are hash-named snapshot files rather than inline text. For each arm of each repetition, materialize a fresh workspace containing every source of the fixture's source corpus (not only the case's changedPaths): write each source's snapshot text verbatim to its corpus-relative path. The snapshot for a source is <snapshotDirectory>/<gitBlobSha1>.txt, where a segmented gitBlobSha1Parts array joins to the 40-hex blob id. Before writing, verify gitBlobSha1(text) equals the manifest blob id, and sha256Text(text) equals the manifest sha256 where the manifest carries one; reject byte drift. Record workspaceTreeSha256 per section 2.2 (SHA-256 over the sorted path + sha256(text) entries). Never reuse a workspace across arms or repetitions; reset between arms.
